newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan overnight rates in 3.50-4.00 percent range.
newsitem.headline: Jordan overnight rates in 3.50-4.00 percent range.

text.p: Overnight rates on the Jordanian dinar eased slightly to a 3.50-4.00 percent range on Thursday from 3.50-4.50 percent on Wednesday with lower borrowing demand by banks, dealers said.
Dealers expect the market to tighten at start of weekly trade on Saturday with some excess funds absorbed by banks subscription in the latest 15 million dinar CD auction.
The Central Bank of Jordan offered banks 15 million dinars in certificates of deposits in this week's auction.
Interest yields released this week from last week's auction for three-month paper were unchanged at 9.250 percent.
Yields on six-month certificates were fixed at 9.500 percent, also unchanged from last week's rate.

Dealers blamed over 13 million dinars in maturing CD's returning to the market behind the excess funds in the market along lower subscription in CDs that helped ease rates in a low 3.50-6.00 range this week.

Outstanding CDs dropped to 514 million dinars from 527.7 million dinars last week. Repurchase agreements as collatoral to weekly CDs remained at a high 10 per cent with an unchanged 8.5 per cent discount rate.
The Central Bank is maintaining a high interest rate policy to preserve the attractiveness of dinar-denominated assets to boost the local currency.
It also wants to curb any excessive outflow of dinars into dollar-denominated assets that could erode its foreign currency reserves.
